title: Yes, Websites Can Detect Your VPN. Here's How
partialText: VPNs hide your IP address and encrypt your traffic, but they don't make you invisible. title: How to Connect AI Agents to Live Web Data With Bright Data's MCP Server
partialText: Your AI agent doesn't have a reasoning problem: it has a vision problem. Without access to live web data, even the smartest model is a well-dressed historian. partialText: A vendor audit found unpinned models running unreviewed remote code via trust_remote_code=True, exposing the AI era's overlooked container supply chain risk.

title: How Small Postgres Metadata Tables Quietly Throttle Your Largest Queries
partialText: Most engineers blame slow time-series queries on massive fact tables, but a small metadata table with stale Postgres statistics can silently become the real bottleneck. This guide shows how outdated ANALYZE data misleads the planner into choosing inefficient joins, how to detect row-estimate mismatches with EXPLAIN, and how to fix them using autovacuum tuning, targeted audits, or selective denormalization.

title: No AI Agent Without Identity (Part 5): Auditability and the Minimum Bar for Governed Autonomy
partialText: Part 5 of a 5-part series on agentic AI governance. This article defines the minimum bar for governed AI autonomy: stable agent identity, ownership, runtime lineage, policy decisions, supervision mode, credential control, revocation behavior, audit evidence, and accountability across human, agent, tool, and context chains.

title: The Compounding Latency Crisis of Multi-Step AI Workflows
partialText: Chaining multiple LLM calls, vector database lookups, and API tools creates a severe performance bottleneck, dragging response times from seconds to minutes. Every sequential step introduces extra network and token processing overhead that quickly ruins the user experience. To fix this compounding latency crisis, engineers must move away from rigid, blocking sequential code. Instead, you need to use smaller, faster models for minor tasks, run speculative database lookups in parallel while models are still thinking, and stream real-time status updates back to the UI to keep the application feeling crisp and responsive.

title: No laptop? No problem. Code on the Go brings the debugger to your phone.
partialText: Traditional Android debugging assumes you have both a computer and a phone. Code on the Go changes that by bringing the entire debugging workflow onto a single Android device. This post explains the technical challenges of building phone-native debugger, including privileged access, process management, and breakpoint handling, and how the team solved them while ensuring the debugger only works on the device running Code on the Go. The result is a fully self-contained Android development experience that lets developers write, build, run, and debug apps anywhere, without a laptop or internet connection.

title: How to Count Gemini Tokens Locally
partialText: This article explores how Gemini tokenizes data and demonstrates how to count or estimate tokens locally. You'll learn how to use the local tokenizer to estimate text token counts offline, understand the tokenization math for multimodal inputs (images, audio, video, PDFs), and see how to retrieve precise token usage metadata from API responses for accurate tracking and billing.

title: Fraud Has Moved Outside the Bank. Protection Should Too
partialText: Banks are investing heavily in cybersecurity and fraud detection, but AI-powered social engineering attacks increasingly happen outside their systems through calls, messages, emails, and social media. Leading institutions like JPMorgan and Revolut are expanding protections with consumer education, scam detection, and intervention tools, yet most defenses still focus on the moment before a transaction occurs. As regulations tighten and fraud losses grow, banks need to move beyond their perimeter and deploy device-level trust layers that can understand communication context, detect scams earlier, and leverage cross-industry threat intelligence to keep pace with AI-enabled fraud at scale.
